title: Modals of Deduction
completion_message: ¡Perfecto! Ahora puedes sacar conclusiones y hacer deducciones profesionales sobre eventos del pasado usando Modales de Deducción.

stages.title: Modales de Deducción en el Pasado

parts.visual:
Usamos modales en pasado (Modal + have + participio) para hacer deducciones sobre cosas que ya pasaron. 
- Must have (Debe haber / Seguro que): Cuando estás 99% seguro de que algo ocurrió. 
Ej: He MUST HAVE SIGNED the contract. (Seguro que firmó / Debe haber firmado).
parts.audio: We use past modals, structure: Modal plus 'have' plus past participle, to make deductions about things that already happened. 'Must have' is used when you are 99% sure that something happened. For example: He must have signed the contract.

parts.visual:
- Might have / May have / Could have (Podría haber / Tal vez): Cuando es posible, pero no estás seguro. 
Ej: They MIGHT HAVE LOST the file. (Tal vez perdieron el archivo). 
- Can't have / Couldn't have (No puede haber / Es imposible que): Cuando estás 99% seguro de que algo NO ocurrió. 
Ej: She COULDN'T HAVE STOLEN the money. (Es imposible que ella haya robado el dinero).
parts.audio: Might have, may have, or could have, are used when it's possible, but you are not sure. For example: They might have lost the file. Can't have or couldn't have, are used when you are 99% sure that something did NOT happen. For example: She couldn't have stolen the money.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el modal de deducción correcto basado en el contexto.

questions.question: The boss is very angry. He ____ found out about the mistake. (Seguro que / Debe haberse enterado).
questions.explanation: Must have: alta certeza de que ocurrió (porque está muy enojado).

questions.question: She ____ stolen the data! She was on vacation in Paris all week. (Es imposible que haya).
questions.explanation: Couldn't have: alta certeza de que NO ocurrió (estaba en París).

questions.question: I can't find my USB drive. I ____ left it at home, but I'm not sure. (Tal vez / Podría haber).
questions.explanation: Might have: posibilidad, pero no hay seguridad ('I'm not sure').

questions.question: They didn't win the contract. They ____ offered a terrible price. (Seguro que).
questions.explanation: Must have: deducción lógica y casi segura.

questions.question: He ____ read my email yet. I only sent it two minutes ago. (Es imposible que haya).
questions.explanation: Can't have: es imposible porque pasó muy poco tiempo.

questions.question: The server crashed. The IT guy ____ made a mistake during the update. (Debe haber).
We ____ won the negotiation, but we walked away too early. (Podríamos haber - pero no lo hicimos).
questions.explanation: Could have: Había la posibilidad en el pasado, pero no sucedió.

questions.question: John didn't come to the meeting. He ____ forgotten about it. (Tal vez - 50% probabilidad).
questions.explanation: May have: es una posibilidad probable.

questions.question: You ____ seen the CEO. He is in Japan right now! (Es imposible que hayas).
questions.explanation: Couldn't have: es imposible, él está en Japón.

questions.question: The presentation was flawless. She ____ prepared for weeks! (Seguro que).
questions.explanation: Must have: deducción lógica por lo impecable que fue.

questions.question: They ____ gone bankrupt. Their profits were up 200% last year! (Es imposible que hayan).
questions.explanation: Can't have: la evidencia (ganancias) contradice la quiebra.

questions.question: I ____ deleted the file by accident, let me check the trash bin. (Tal vez).
He has a new Ferrari. He ____ received a massive bonus! (Seguro que).
questions.explanation: Must have: deducción lógica ante la nueva riqueza.

questions.question: The client didn't sign. They ____ liked our proposal. (Seguro que NO).
questions.explanation: Must not have: Deducción lógica negativa (Seguro que no les gustó). Can't have es 'es imposible que les haya gustado', que es muy fuerte aquí.

questions.question: We sent the package on Monday. They ____ received it by now. (Deberían haber - expectativa lógica).
questions.explanation: Should have: expectativa lógica (no deducción 100% segura, sino lo que 'debería' ser).

questions.question: The office is completely dark. Everyone ____ gone home. (Seguro que se han).
She speaks fluent Mandarin. She ____ lived in China. (Seguro que / Debe haber).
questions.explanation: Must have: Deducción por su fluidez.

questions.question: You ____ sent that angry email to the client. Now we lost the deal. (No deberías haber - crítica).
questions.explanation: Shouldn't have: se usa para criticar o arrepentirse de una acción pasada.

questions.question: He looks exhausted. He ____ been working all night. (Seguro que ha).
questions.explanation: Must have been working (deducción continua en el pasado).

questions.question: I don't know why the system failed. It ____ been a virus, but I will check. (Podría haber).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe el modal correcto (must, might, can't, could) seguido de 'have'.

questions.question: He is angry. He ____ have found out. (Seguro que)
She is in Paris. She ____ have stolen it. (Es imposible / can't)
I'm not sure. I ____ have lost it. (Tal vez / might)
They didn't win. They ____ have offered a bad price. (Seguro que)
You sent it 1 minute ago. He ____ have read it yet. (Es imposible / couldn't)
The server crashed. The IT guy ____ have made a mistake. (Seguro que)
We walked away. We ____ have won, but we didn't try. (Podríamos)
He didn't come. He ____ have forgotten. (Tal vez / may)
He has a Ferrari. He ____ have gotten a bonus. (Seguro que)
You lost the client! You ____ not have sent that angry email! (No deberías - crítica)

pairs.target: Es imposible que ella lo haya hecho
